For Hilbert-valued i.i.d. observations, the $L^2$ prediction error bound has an order of $O(n^{-1/2})$, with no dimension factor or restriction on covariance eigenvalue decay, and the same coupling retains bounds for every spectral projection. In an $\ell^2$ example, we demonstrate that the coordinate-wise error gives sharp error order of $n^{-1/2}$.

papers.title: Fast and Scalable Abstract Interpretation for Deep Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Abstract interpretation can certify properties of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), but precise analyses remain expensive. General implementations repeat work when analyzing the same architecture under different inputs and properties. Interleaving this work with numerical operations limits GPU utilization and restricts how much of the analysis a tensor compiler can process together. We present Scepter, a framework for specializing DNN abstract interpreters through structural semantics. The semantics determine the structure of intermediate abstract values while deferring their numerical evaluation. Structural computations from successive operations can therefore be performed together before certification, generating an executable tensor program. With the abstract interpreter and DNN architecture fixed, the program can be reused with different weights and input regions. We prove that it computes the same bounds as the general interpreter in exact arithmetic. The generated program also exposes operations and their dependencies for tensor compilation and memory planning. We implement Scepter for the tensor programs that Neuton generates from ConstraintFlow specifications. We evaluate Scepter on eight abstract interpreters and 44 DNNs against six baseline systems on GPUs and CPUs. Scepter handles networks with up to 153x as many neurons as the largest completed by the corresponding baselines. It completes DeepPoly on ResNet50 and VGG-16, whereas none of the evaluated DeepPoly baselines completes either network. On configurations completed by both systems, GPU geometric-mean speedups over Neuton range from 11.9x to 44.4x across eight analyses, with a 2.60x geometric-mean reduction in peak memory. In an input-splitting case study, Scepter proves 68 properties for which the baselines time out. Code: https://github.com/uiuc-focal-lab/constraintflow.git

papers.title: Z-Boson Production in Proton-Lead Collisions with MRW Nuclear TMDs
papers.abstract: The production of dileptons in proton-lead collisions probes the transverse-momentum structure of partons in a nuclear environment. We summarize a $k_t$-factorization study of $Z$ boson production at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=8.16\,\mathrm{TeV}$, comparing transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distributions constructed with leading-order and Next-to-leading-order Martin-Ryskin-Watt (LO-MRW and NLO-MRW) prescriptions. Parton-level predictions obtained with \textsc{KaTie} are confronted with the CMS measurements in two invariant-mass regions, using the dilepton transverse momentum, $φ^*_η$ and center-of-mass rapidity. The models describe the overall trends near the $Z$ resonance, while the virtuality constraint in NLO-MRW changes the high-transverse-momentum behavior. At lower dilepton masses, both prescriptions underestimate parts of the data, particularly the NLO-MRW result. These comparisons illustrate both the potential and the limitations of last-step-evolution nuclear TMD models for $Z$ boson production in proton-nucleus collisions.

papers.title: RecordRoute: Auditing Agent Failures with Localization-Guided Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Auditing failed agent executions requires identifying the responsible actor, the earliest decisive step, and the error mode. Representative supervised methods either focus on step localization or predict multiple attribution targets from shared trajectory representations. These methods do not use the localization result to select the text for mode diagnosis. To address this limitation, we propose RecordRoute, which couples comparative localization with local diagnosis. Specifically, it represents each record with word and character features and learns to rank records through comparisons within each trajectory. The selected record supplies the actor and step, while its text and metadata drive mode prediction. On controlled-injection Who&When Pro, RecordRoute outperforms StepFinder and ASCon on all four official metrics. With actor and step predictions fixed, local diagnosis reaches 77.47% pooled joint accuracy versus 69.28% for full-trace diagnosis. On natural failures from TraceElephant and CatchBench POST, it outperforms these baselines and three open LLMs in localization.

papers.title: PAC-style Bounds on the Conditional Validity of Conformal Predictors
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction sets are guaranteed to be marginally valid over the attribute space, but local coverage can diverge from the user-defined target $1-α$. Constructing conditionally valid prediction sets with finite calibration data is impossible for a general data-generating distribution. We derive PAC-type probabilistic lower bounds on the input-conditional coverage of any conformal predictor, without assumptions on the data distribution. They are based on the Markov and Cantelli inequalities and adapt to both calibration-marginal and calibration-conditional setups. A tighter, model-dependent Cantelli bound depends on the variance of the conditional coverage and is estimable from data using a fully non-asymptotic Hoeffding argument. The results suggest conditional-coverage variance as a scalable and theoretically motivated empirical measure of conditional validity.

papers.title: Best Arm Identification with Unknown Post-Action Context Distribution
papers.abstract: We study best arm identification (BAI) with post-action context in the fixed-confidence setting. After choosing an action, the learner observes a post-action context together with a reward whose distribution depends only on this context. Incorporating such intermediate information can substantially reduce the sample complexity of identifying the best arm. While Shahverdikondori et al. (2026a) analyzed the case where the distribution of contexts given actions is known, we address the more challenging and practically relevant case where this distribution is unknown. We derive an instance-dependent sample complexity lower bound and propose a Track-and-Stop algorithm that matches it asymptotically with access to an optimization oracle. Our stopping rule uses a new concentration inequality that jointly controls uncertainty in the context distributions and reward means, removing the factor of two incurred by separate concentration bounds. Implementing the algorithm generally requires solving nonconvex optimization problems. We propose a convex relaxation with instance-dependent approximation guarantees, including asymptotic tightness on hard Gaussian instances. Experiments demonstrate that exploiting post-action context reduces the sample complexity relative to baselines that ignore it, even when the context distributions are unknown.

papers.title: Bloch Discriminants of Discrete Periodic Operators
papers.abstract: The Bloch variety of an operator on a periodic graph encodes the relation between its spectrum and the group action on the graph, with critical points corresponding to edges of the spectrum. We adapt methods from computational algebraic geometry to describe how the qualitative behavior of critical points of Bloch varieties depends upon parameters for three Z^2-periodic graphs. The set of parameters where the qualitative behavior changes is the Bloch discriminant. As the critical points are real-algebraic with respect to a non-standard real structure on the complex torus, this is also a first step towards developing computational tools for varieties with a non-standard real structure.

papers.title: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain
papers.abstract: We introduce the first score-based generative model for signals on a fixed hypergraph, formulated in the spectral domain of t-product hypergraph signal processing (t-HGSP). The naive tensor heat semigroup is ill-posed, since after palindromic symmetrization the spectral slices of the Laplacian tensor are no longer positive semidefinite. A per-mode frequency shift repairs it, yielding a forward Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion that decouples per (eigenmode, slice) pair with closed-form marginals, exact score targets, and an exactly isotropic stationary law. A lightweight slice-conditioned denoiser is trained on the resulting real spectral grid. Sampling combines its score on data-active modes with the closed-form score elsewhere, which proves essential for stability at scale. A closed cosine-form observation operator turns missing-node recovery into linear-Gaussian guidance with stabilized posterior sampling. On hypergraphs of up to 500 nodes, our model beats a clique-expansion baseline by margins growing from $2\times$ to $27\times$ in covariance error, matches the graph-spectral statistics of the data better than the graph-basis model itself, and reaches the finite-sample estimation floor on data rotated off the t-spectral axes. Posterior sampling reduces missing-node NMSE to 0.28-0.64 (classical baselines 0.87-1.1) at conservative coverage, and cuts the framework's own denoising baseline by up to $3.6\times$.

papers.title: Polynomial Master Equations of Open Quantum Systems and an Analysis on the Critical Solutions
papers.abstract: The dynamics of open quantum systems exhibits in general a non-Markovian behavior, lying typically beyond the description of first-order differential equations. Traditional methods commonly turned to first-order integro-differential equations, which allowed for the standard interpretation of non-Markovianity as having its origin in the global history of the system evolution. We examine the possibility of an alternative, locally deterministic interpretation [arXiv:2607.09651] of the working of its dynamical hysteresis, where the evolution of a system is determined by its local behavior alone. The present work elaborates on our systematic method in deriving non-Markovian linear differential equations associated with matrix polynomials of higher order. Our methods will be demonstrated with exact analyses on two illustrative examples: one built upon the simplest non-trivial model concerning a two-qubit system, and another involving an unbounded Hamiltonian defined on an infinite-dimensional quantum system. We also analyze the critical parameters at which qualitative changes are observed in the system dynamics, and reveal how our polynomial equations account for the phenomena.

papers.title: High-Performance Algorithms for Computing the V-BLAST Permutation
papers.abstract: We propose two novel and efficient algorithms for computing a column permutation called V-BLAST or an approximation of it. The V-BLAST column permutation is used in a QR factorization that is part of an integer/discrete least-squares solver. The overall solver is part of the receiver in advanced communication systems that transmit multiple symbols simultaneously. Two classes of efficient algorithms for computing the exact V-BLAST permutation have been proposed in the literature. The first, based on a sequence of Givens rotations, is unfortunately highly sequential. The other, based on a sequence of downdating operations on a pseudo-inverse, has a shorter critical path, but is unlikely to be numerically stable. The new algorithms that we propose are inspired by the similarity between V-BLAST and rank-revealing QR factorizations. Our first algorithm uses Householder reflections, is numerically stable, and has a short critical path. It is unable, however, to efficiently exploit cache memories. We rectify this with a randomized algorithm that computes an approximation to the V-BLAST permutation and has a short critical path and can effectively exploit cache memories. We prove approximation properties of the randomized algorithm and demonstrate experimentally that both algorithms are faster than existing ones, both when tested in isolation and when tested within an integer least-squares solver.

papers.title: Prismatic construction of crystalline deformation rings up to p-power torsion
papers.abstract: We study the deformation of Galois representations which are etale realizations of finitely generated prismatic F-crystals and show the deformation functor is pro-represented by a complete Noetherian local ring whose Z_p-flat quotient coincides with Kisin's crystalline deformation ring. As a consequence, we obtain a universal prismatic F-crystal with coefficients in Kisin's crystalline deformation ring.

papers.title: SALSA: Sampling Adversarial Suffixes from Learned Distributions for LLM Safety Assessment
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, where adversaries append optimized suffixes to otherwise benign looking prompts to bypass safety alignment. Existing optimization-based GCG-style attacks can be effective, but they are expensive at inference time, and suffer from poor transfer. We present, SALSA, a generative framework that learns a distribution over jailbreak suffixes from optimization-derived attack corpora. Once trained, the model supports efficient sampling-based attacks. On open-source targets, it achieves attack success rates comparable to state-of-the-art optimization baselines, while reducing generation time from 3.46s to 0.04s per prompt. In black-box transfer, it remains highly effective against proprietary systems, including 99% ASR on GPT-3.5-Turbo, and reaches 45% ASR on the substantially harder GPT-4o, more than doubling the strongest baseline at an equal sampling budget. We further offer an intuition for why generative sampling can preserve high attack success, when the learned suffix distribution is close to the distribution of optimization outputs. Overall, our results show that learning adversarial suffix distributions yields a scalable, and practically efficient foundation for continuous LLM vulnerability discovery.

papers.title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?
papers.abstract: We give four large language models (LLMs) of the Claude family the complete weights of a 20k-parameter CIFAR-10 CNN as text and ask them to produce a 4-bit network without tools, data or the ability to run inference. Standard round-to-nearest (RTN) quantization to 4 bit lowers the test accuracy from 81.4% to 60.4%. We design four evaluation protocols that differ in the input and task description given to the LLMs and analyze their responses. In the first two protocols the LLMs are given the float and the 4-bit RTN network and are told that the accuracy has dropped significantly. In the last two they receive only the float network and the task to quantize it, which tests whether they apply an optimization on their own or fall back to plain RTN. Our analysis shows that a frontier LLM can recover most of the lost accuracy. Given one answer per layer, Opus 5.5 raises the accuracy of the 4-bit network to 77.95% by balancing the rounding errors within each 3x3 kernel, reasoning over the integer weights without tools. This is 3.5 pp below the float network and 2.8 pp below AdaRound, which learns the rounding from calibration data. Given only the float network, the LLMs name error-cancelling corrections but do not apply them and fall back to plain RTN, at most with mildly clipped scales, which still lifts Fable 5.2's quantized network to 70.0%. We analyze in detail what the LLMs did and why it works. Code and prompts can be found at https://github.com/urbste/weight-space-programming-ptq

papers.title: SHARPnP: Self-Supervised and Plug-and-Play Hyperspectral Super-Resolution from Real Noisy Unaligned Camera Measurements
papers.abstract: Affordable snapshot hyperspectral cameras capture spectral images in a single exposure but suffer from limited spatial resolution and sensor noise. Low-cost RGB cameras provide fine visible details to guide NIR reconstruction, but introduce spatially varying cross-camera misalignment. Supervised fusion methods require relatively large datasets of clean, high-resolution hyperspectral images, are sensitive to sensor noise, and generalize poorly across new sensors. We introduce SHARPnP, an interpretable, flexible framework coupling registration and reconstruction for RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution from noisy, unaligned measurements without clean references. We adapt a pretrained registration model via a cross-view loss backpropagated through a fixed plug-and-play fusion module. Temporal and recorrupted pairs enable reference-free self-supervision on noisy inputs. At test time, we calibrate cross-camera radiometry and refine alignment. Plug-and-play fusion employs sequential three-band denoising. On the REAL benchmark, SHARPnP outperforms supervised fusion baselines at $4\times$, $8\times$, and $16\times$ on clean inputs and at $4\times$ under Gaussian noise ($σ=5/255, 10/255$). On native RGB-HSI snapshot measurements, it reconstructs all 51 VIS-NIR bands, beyond the conventional 31-band VIS setting, without high-resolution references.

papers.title: Scalar-tensor interactions selected through their first-order thermodynamic dynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate the restrictive capability of first-order thermodynamics on scalar-tensor gravity. Starting from a general action containing nonlinear curvature dependence, an Einstein-tensor-Hessian coupling, and independent quadratic and cubic scalar-Hessian interactions, we derive the complete effective-fluid quantities. Simultaneously imposing Eckart's heat-conduction and shear-viscosity equations, while accounting for cancellations between interactions, substantially reduces the original operator basis and determines the geometric shear viscosity. Retaining the complete heat-conduction law, we establish an integrability condition that constrains the nonlinear Hessian interactions without prescribing the temperature and thermal conductivity. We construct explicit constitutive pairs and derive the associated thermal evolution, revealing contributions beyond the usual acceleration-aligned description. Remarkably, the thermodynamic integrability condition simplifies the scalar-metric kinetic structure such that imposing covariant degeneracy excludes the remaining nonlinear interactions, recovering the established luminal Horndeski subclass. Nonlinear thermodynamically compatible interactions nevertheless survive when degeneracy is restricted to the scalar-unitary gauge. These results establish a connection between thermodynamic integrability and dynamical degeneracy, demonstrating the potential of first-order thermodynamics as an independent and complementary criterion for selecting gravitational interactions.

papers.title: Quantitative $p$-Wasserstein bounds for empirical measures on manifolds: Expectation and concentration
papers.abstract: We derive quantitative bounds in expectation and concentration for the $p$-Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of independent samples and their common law on metric measure spaces satisfying the measure contraction property $\MCP(K,n)$, with $K\le0$. Our results extend the expectation estimates of Boissard--Le Gouic (Theorem 1.1 in Ann. Inst. Henri Poincaré Probab. Stat. 50 (2014), no. 2, 539--563) and the concentration estimates of Bolley--Guillin--Villani (Theorem 2.1 in Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 137 (2007), 541--593). In spaces with exponential volume growth, suitable exponential moment assumptions allow us to recover the Euclidean rate $N^{-1/n}$ in expectation when $n>2p$. As an application, we obtain uniform-in-time concentration estimates for the empirical measure of McKean--Vlasov interacting particle systems on complete Riemannian manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below by combining comparison theory and parallel coupling to a noninteracting proxy system.

papers.title: Hybrid AI for AI-Native RAN Control: A Functional Perspective
papers.abstract: AI-native radio access network (RAN) control involves interdependent decisions across network entities, protocol layers, and timescales. Understanding how AI and conventional methods can jointly support these decisions requires a common basis for comparing their functional roles. This survey introduces a technique-agnostic taxonomy of RAN decision-making organized around four complementary capabilities: Representation and Reasoning, Prediction and Simulation, Adaptive Control, and Decision Synthesis. These capabilities are defined by their roles in the control process, independently of the techniques used to implement them. Through this perspective, we examine representative AI and model-based approaches, including foundation models, world models, reinforcement learning, and optimization. We then apply the taxonomy to representative RAN control solutions across slow, medium, fast, and cross-timescale applications to identify which capabilities they implement and how these capabilities are combined in hybrid AI systems. We also review datasets, benchmarks, simulators, digital twins, and experimental platforms according to their support for the decision-making process and reproducible evaluation. The review highlights a gap between the availability of resources for closed-loop experimentation and the standardization of tasks, metrics, and evaluation protocols needed for meaningful comparisons.Finally, we identify research directions for hybrid AI in AI-native RAN, including capability integration, multi-agent and cross-timescale coordination, constraint handling, and reproducible closed-loop evaluation. A curated list of surveyed works and evaluation resources is available at https://github.com/pegahani/Hybrid-AI-RAN-Survey.

papers.title: Towards Realistic Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantification for LLM-Based Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a flexible interface for recommendation systems. However, their issued rankings require reliable instance-level uncertainty monitoring. In this scenario, comparing uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods becomes challenging because LLM rankers lack a standard item-classification head. Their scores may depend on option labels, prompts, generation procedures, and the available user and item evidence. Existing methods derive uncertainty from different sources and apply it at different stages of the recommendation process. Some methods evaluate an issued ranking, whereas others use uncertainty to change the ranking itself, making direct comparison difficult. Here we introduce a fixed-ranking benchmark which evaluates eight heterogeneous UQ signals as record-level monitors under a shared output contract. We evaluate these signals across four recommendation datasets and two LLM backbones under a shared fixed-ranking protocol. From the results, we draw three main observations. First, UQ method ordering changes across backbones even on the same reference instances. Second, ranking-aligned Top10Mass provides the strongest scalar Error@10 detection in several evaluation conditions, reflecting effective cutoff-aligned monitoring, while its advantage narrows for popularity-tail targets. Third, scalar UQ signals are weak at identifying which control has the larger clipped NDCG@10 difference, whereas source-specific signals, including Perturbation Rank Instability and simple listwise distances, provide stronger paired-control agreement, reflecting their sensitivity to the two controlled evidence sources. These findings motivate us to evaluate ranking-failure detection, robustness across recommendation conditions, and responses to controlled evidence changes as distinct properties of UQ.

papers.title: Linear Probes Can Guide: Training-Free Control of Representation Generators
papers.abstract: Representation-space generative models, such as Representation Autoencoders (RAEs), leverage pretrained vision foundation models (VFMs) primarily to accelerate training and improve sample fidelity. Yet VFMs are more than reconstruction tokenizers, as they feature rich representation spaces that are highly organized and linearly readable. We observe that this removes a key obstacle of post-hoc guidance: by linearity of expectation, a clean probe applied to an ideal denoiser's prediction yields the exact posterior mean of the probe scores at any noise level. This regime, which we call Semantic Mean-Space, turns semantic guidance into a Bayesian linear inverse problem, bypassing the need for training-time conditioning. With this foundation, we propose LiSM, a unified framework for Linear Guidance in Semantic Mean-Space. To validate the framework, we developed and adapted different solvers, and characterized them based on how they estimate probe-space uncertainty and propagate the correction through the representation. In addition, we propose Fit-Path, a solver designed to achieve strong global and local control. Our results in four control setups (class, attributes, foreground, and keypoints) show that LiSM methods, and Fit-Path in particular, provide effective, lightweight control across global and local tasks, outperforming noise-aware and pixel-space guidance.

papers.title: The Poissonian limit of a model inspired by the one-dimensional ERAP, and its application to satellite data
papers.abstract: We consider a model of particle tracking in one dimension studied by Quarck in which $n$ independent random points of the interval $[0,1]$ are shifted by i.i.d. noise at a common scale $\varepsilon_n>0$. We prove that, if $\varepsilon_n=αn^{-2}+\mathbf{o}(n^{-2})$ for some $α>0$ when $n\to \infty$, then in the latter limit the total number of consecutive swaps in the shifted sample w.r.t. its order statistics converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with a parameter depending explicitly on the product of $α$, the mean absolute difference of the shifts and the $L^2$-norm of the density of points. We compare the statistical criterion implied by this theorem to numerical simulations based on real terrain maps, and discuss both its usefulness and limitations.

papers.title: Certifying total-variation contamination by betting on trimmed kernel witnesses
papers.abstract: Two laws share a common component after each discards a fraction $α$ of its mass, a trimming, exactly when their total variation is at most $α$, so the contamination level $α^\star = \mathrm{TV} (P,Q)$ is the share of each population without counterpart in the other. We bound it from below from two samples on any space with a bounded characteristic kernel. The kernel mean embeddings of all such trimmings of a law form a convex region, the regions of two laws first touch at $α^\star$, and in every direction a region reaches as far as a trimmed mean. The difference of their closest points, the witness, selects the trimming. We fit a ramp of the witness on part of the data and bet on the rest, at each level of a grid. The bound is valid at every sample size. The cut points of the tested level carry most of its finite-sample gain over an untrimmed witness, while refitting the witness at that level makes it consistent, gives its rates and returns the trimming. When a function of the kernel's Hilbert space separates the parts of the two laws without counterpart, the bound is within order $(n\wedge m)^{-1/2}$ of $α^\star$ on a grid of that mesh, which is minimax over such pairs. When these parts touch, a margin condition guarantees a polynomial rate for Sobolev kernels and a logarithmic rate for the Gaussian kernel. For the Laplace kernel on the line this guarantee is not sharp: the witness stays between its two cut points, and for densities that cross once, with a likelihood ratio bounded away from one off the crossing, the error on such a grid is again of that order up to logarithmic factors. No informative upper bound exists without assumptions. On the Right Heart Catheterization data, with confidence $0.95$, each arm must lose more than a fraction $0.35$ of its patients, if both lose the same fraction, before their covariate distributions can coincide.

papers.title: At the Limit: Autonomous Vehicle Drifting under Generative Policies
papers.abstract: Autonomous drifting requires agile control despite tire-force saturation and highly nonlinear vehicle dynamics. We propose an online reinforcement learning method for flow policies that combines stochastic differential equation (SDE) sampling for exploration with value-based policy optimization. This method supports both training from scratch and fine-tuning a policy pretrained on expert demonstrations. After training, control actions can be generated using either SDEs or ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Experiments on circular and eight-shaped drifting in an F1TENTH digital twin platform show that both training strategies can achieve effective real-time drift control, with tighter tracking, higher success rates, and better robustness under noisy conditions.

papers.title: Multistable Thermoelectric Josephson Automata
papers.abstract: Multistable systems can store and process information, yet their elements usually only burn the drive energy. Here, we build an automaton whose elements actively convert heat into electrical power. Heat alone stabilizes the states at zero bias, and each state routes generation and dissipation to different junctions. The elements, gap-asymmetric superconducting tunnel junctions, deliver up to 2.6 pW at either polarity under fixed heating and support a magnetic-field-tunable Josephson current. Two junctions sharing a heated island split the bias hysteretically and, even at zero bias, lock into opposite voltages encoding the sweep direction. With a load and current bias, the automaton accesses states spanning junction polarity combinations, including zero voltage; the magnetic field sets which are available and the bias history selects the occupied one.

papers.title: Spectrify: Framework for Hyperspectral Image Generation Using Computer Graphics
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) record the full spectrum of light at every pixel, so projecting an HSI through a camera's spectral sensitivities gives that camera's RAW image, and one HSI can supply training data for hyperspectral reconstruction and camera-pipeline methods. Real HSIs, however, are slow and expensive to capture, and the largest datasets hold only about 1,000 images. High-level vision commonly replaces scarce real data with images rendered from 3D scenes. Low-level tasks, however, need physically correct spectra, which requires spectral rendering with a measured spectrum for every material in a scene, and existing spectral renderings cover only a handful of scenes, mostly with a simplified image formation model. We present Spectrify, a framework that converts 3D scene datasets into HSIs, together with a library of reflectance spectra labeled by material and compiled from close-range hyperspectral datasets and spectrophotometer measurements. In Spectrify, spectra follow the material: each object receives a physically based optical model and measured reflectance spectra or optical constants from its material category, each lamp an emission spectrum of its type and the sky a modeled daylight spectrum, and Mitsuba 3 path-traces the full light transport of each scene per wavelength. We show that a hyperspectral reconstruction network trained only on our synthetic HSIs generalizes to unseen real datasets better than networks trained on the largest real HSI datasets on most test sets, and that assigning spectra by material category instead of by color alone improves this transfer on every test set. RAW images projected from our HSIs are also useful training data for color constancy, performing on par with existing synthetic RAW generators. We release the 4,500 rendered HSIs, the code of Spectrify and its material-labeled reflectance library.

papers.title: A unified approach to logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski inequalities and logarithmic Minkowski problems for geometric functionals
papers.abstract: We establish two general principles for geometric functionals, one for proving logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequalities and the other for solving the associated logarithmic Minkowski problems. For origin-symmetric convex bodies, we prove logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, spectral zeta functions, torsional rigidity, and chord integrals, along with their equality conditions. For each functional, we give the necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of an origin-symmetric solution to the corresponding logarithmic Minkowski problem for even measures and prove uniqueness.

papers.title: When Is Product Decoding of ECOC MAP-Consistent? Pair Structure and the n-vs-Rest Codes
papers.abstract: Error-Correcting Output Codes (ECOC) combine binary classifiers by the sum decoder, which totals probabilities, or the product decoder, which totals log-likelihoods. In the noiseless setting, where the binary classifiers output the true posteriors, we ask on which code matrices each decoder always agrees with the Bayes-optimal (MAP) class. For the sum decoder the answer is known: the code must be equidistant (James and Hastie, 1998). We answer the question for the product decoder. Two classes are compared through the votes of the columns on which they differ: the sum decoder decides by their sample mean, the product decoder by an M-estimator with influence function artanh, and each vote is the MAP margin plus a bias determined by the other classes alone. Our main theorem states that the product decoder is MAP-consistent if and only if, for every class pair, the columns on which the two classes differ are matched with the columns obtained by swapping the two classes (or their complements), and equivalently if and only if the code is a union of n-vs-Rest codes. Efficient equidistant codes are therefore excluded: Hadamard codes ($M\ge 8$), which meet the Plotkin bound with $M-1$ columns, have no such pairs, and for the Sylvester type the reversal margin can be at least a constant 0.0182 independent of $M$. All theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4. On six real datasets with estimated probabilities, the product decoder is slightly more accurate when each column is calibrated, and the sum decoder is better when the calibration error differs across columns; in either case the decoders disagree only near ties.

papers.title: A Bernstein-Type Variance-Adaptive PMW Mechanism for DP Query Release
papers.abstract: Private Multiplicative Weights (PMW) is a central mechanism for the differentially private release of adaptive linear statistics over a finite universe. Its classical analysis uses a fixed multiplicative-weights learning rate and does not exploit the local variance of the current hypothesis. This paper presents PMW-Bernstein, a variance-adaptive refinement in which the update step is determined by the relationship between the privately estimated query error and the variance under the current hypothesis. The mechanism retains the standard PMW privacy architecture based on Sparse Vector screening, Gaussian numerical measurements, sequential composition, and post-processing. Through a potential-based analysis, we prove a one-step progress bound that yields a global weighted energy bound, recovers the classical $O(1/α2)$ update regime in general, and establishes an $O(1/α)$ update regime under a Bernsteintype condition on updated rounds. Controlled simulations over synthetic finite-universe distributions and query workloads show that the adaptive rule reduces the number of updates in the low-variance regime, remains competitive in the high-variance regime, and succeeds within the prescribed update budget in the heterogeneous regime where the fixed-step baseline fails.

papers.title: Undershoot of h-fold sumsets: Apéry spectra, similar ordering and the three-distance theorem
papers.abstract: For a finite set $A_0\subset\mathbb{N}$ with $0\in A_0$, $\max A_0=d$ and $\gcd(A_0)=1$, and a target $T$, the undershoot at level $h$ is the distance from $T$ down to the largest element of the $h$-fold sumset $hA_0$ not above $T$. Its total over $T\in[0,hd]$ is bounded in $h$: for large $h$ it equals the sum of the masses of two numerical semigroups attached to $A_0$, where the mass adds $L(L+1)/2$ over the maximal runs of $L$ gaps. We describe how the total reaches this limit: it can rise to it, fall to it, or climb past it and return. When the monomial curve of $A_0$ is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, two Apéry sets give every undershoot exactly, and partial sums of a fixed spectrum bound the total from below, with equality at every level exactly when two threshold sequences are similarly ordered; the total then rises concavely to its limit, reached exactly at the sumsets regularity. We characterize the similarly ordered four-element sets. For $\{0,a,b,2b\}$ with $0<a<b$ coprime, the three-distance theorem gives the total in explicit quadratic pieces. A non-Cohen-Macaulay set exceeds its limit at every failing level $h$ with $hd$ at least the sum of the two conductors; every such four-element set does so, and a five-element example never does. For arbitrary sets, finite corner data give the exact undershoot over any window.

papers.title: Stochastic Taylor expansions for Volterra equations and their geometry
papers.abstract: We develop series representations for solutions to general nonlinear controlled and stochastic Volterra equations in terms of two new types of signature, called geometric and Itô Volterra signature. These signatures collect the necessary iterated kernel integrals and satisfy (quasi) shuffle identities, which allow us to prove universal approximation results for Volterra path functionals. We then derive finite order expansions with precise remainder terms for both controlled and stochastic Volterra equations with possibly singular kernels, as well as expansions of their expectations. For the latter, we provide sufficient conditions for absolute convergence of the resulting series representation and verify them for polynomial Volterra processes. As an application, we propose a weak approximation principle for stochastic Volterra equations based on matching low-order expected signature coordinates of the kernel. Numerical experiments for Volterra-Jacobi processes demonstrate promising performance.

papers.title: Latent Merger: Latent-Space Composition of Hypernetwork-Generated LoRAs
papers.abstract: Recent work proposes hypernetworks that convert a document into a low-rank parameter update (LoRA) in a single forward pass, enabling fast injection of new knowledge into a frozen LLM. However, storing separate LoRA adapters for each document can be unsustainable in streaming settings. In this paper, we study the problem of composing hypernetwork-generated LoRAs using two representative systems, Doc-to-LoRA and SHINE. We show that hypernetwork-generated LoRAs have a geometry sharply different from directly fine-tuned LoRAs. They exhibit greater spectral concentration and stronger cross-document alignment than next-token prediction and QA fine-tuned adapters, which are diffuse and nearly orthogonal across documents. Guided by this observation, we propose latent-space LoRA merging. We compose the intermediate hypernetwork latents and then decode the merged latent through the frozen LoRA-generation head. We show that latent-space merging techniques consistently improve over weight-space and factor-space baselines while preserving a single fixed-rank adapter. These results support latent-space composition as a promising mechanism for combining hypernetwork-generated LoRAs under a fixed output-rank budget.

papers.title: Nonlinear non-modal stability and minimal perturbations in electroconvection driven by unipolar injection
papers.abstract: Electroconvection in a dielectric liquid subjected to unipolar charge injection is subcritical. Convection can be sustained well below the threshold of linear stability theory, and experiments report onset far below it. We use nonlinear non-modal optimization to determine the smallest charge perturbations that trigger convection below the linear threshold. The method, based on a direct--adjoint formulation of the full electrohydrodynamic equations, recovers the classical linear threshold in the limit of small amplitudes. At finite amplitude, the most dangerous perturbations are localized charge deficits rather than excesses, because a deficit relaxes more slowly under Coulomb repulsion. The minimal perturbation needed for transition grows from about 0.5% of the injected charge near the linear threshold to 3% at two thirds of it, where the convective branch ends, in agreement with direct numerical simulations. Near the critical amplitude, trajectories approach an unstable steady state, the edge state, that separates the basins of attraction of rest and convection and originates from the critical linear mode. The damped oscillatory modes involved in the growth of the optimal perturbations are transit-time modes of the ion drift. The convective mode is the first of them, made stationary by the coupling with the flow, which explains why the instability sets in as a steady motion. Small charge fluctuations can therefore lower the onset of electroconvection to about two thirds of the linear threshold, helping to explain the discrepancy between linear theory and experiments.

papers.title: Worth the Wait? How Response Time and Streaming Shape Judgments of Generative AI Answers and Chatbot Engagement
papers.abstract: Answers from generative AI chatbots built on large language models (LLMs) now arrive at very different speeds: reasoning models deliberate before replying, while response caches can return a stored answer at once. Blind preference votes, which rank these models, are read as judgments of their text, and if delivery matters, faster answers are expected to gain. Research on the labor illusion and on how text appears on screen suggests instead that an answer which unfolds as it is written is credited over the same answer shown at once. We test these accounts with three sources of variation in natural use. First, compar:IA, a French government chatbot arena, answered repeated prompts, by a random draw, either with a fresh answer streamed as it was written or with a stored earlier answer from the same model, shown at once. Within the same prompt, a replay lowered an answer's chance of winning a decisive blind vote by 25.8 percentage points. The same stored text won 57% of its decisive votes when streamed and 29% when replayed, and voters called it less complete, more superficial and more often incorrect when replayed. Second, provider congestion slowed streamed answers. In 324,029 conversations, slower answers earned no detectable net credit in the vote, but a slower first exchange made visitors less likely to ask a follow-up question. Third, in 4,378,514 WildChat replies from everyday ChatGPT use, replies slowed by congestion made users less likely to continue. Delivery moved blind votes, in the direction opposite to the one the arena's designers expected, while waiting cost follow-up questions that a comparison between two answers cannot register when both are slow. The results bear on how AI services cache and stream answers, how they budget latency, and how preference leaderboards evaluate models.

papers.title: Approximate MMS allocations for large number of agents
papers.abstract: We consider allocation of indivisible items to agents with non-negative additive valuations, under the maximin share (MMS) fairness benchmark. We prove that for every $ρ< 1$, there exists some $n_ρ$ such that every allocation instance with $n \ge n_ρ$ agents has a $ρ$-MMS allocation. This was explicitly stated as a conjecture in a recent paper of the authors, where it was shown to hold if the number of items is at most $(2 - ε)n$ (and $n \ge n_{ρ, ε}$). We build on some techniques from that earlier paper, including the construction of $\textit{ordinal MMS}$ allocations that give $n - O(\log^2 n)$ agents their full MMS. Among the new techniques that we introduce is the definition of $\textit{block-matchings}$ between the MMS partitions of two agents, and a proof that if the number of item types is small, then block-matchings of small width necessarily exist.

papers.title: $(1-\varepsilon)$-MMS Allocations
papers.abstract: We study maximin share (MMS) allocations of $m$ indivisible items among $n$ agents with additive valuations. We prove that for both goods and chores, the optimal MMS approximation factor converges to $1$ as $n$ grows. In particular, for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, sufficiently large $n$, and any $m$, we give polynomial-time algorithms that compute a $(1-\varepsilon)$-MMS allocation for goods and a $(1+\varepsilon)$-MMS allocation for chores. Furthermore, both algorithms can be implemented using a polynomial number of bundle comparisons.

papers.title: General-relativistic Vlasov disks in external magnetic fields around Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate stationary general-relativistic kinetic models of a collisionless gas around the Kerr black hole immersed in an external magnetic field. The main focus is put on razor-thin disks confined to the equatorial plane, but geometrically thick disks are also briefly mentioned. We consider distribution functions corresponding to constant canonical energy and constant canonical angular momentum of particles within the disk and obtain analytic expressions for the electric current associated with the gas. More general solutions characterized by distribution functions depending on the energy and the angular momentum are obtained assuming the Schwarzschild background metric. In explicit examples, we investigate disks in the Wald magnetosphere, describing an asymptotically uniform magnetic field.

papers.title: EmbodiSafety: Benchmarking Risk Understanding and Response in Embodied AI
papers.abstract: Progress in embodied foundation models is largely measured by task success, while the physical safety of their decisions remains underexamined. Safety evaluations centered on rule following and binary judgments do not adequately assess whether embodied models understand environmental hazards and make safe decisions. We introduce EmbodiSafety, comprising 1,092 snapshot tasks and 540 trajectory tasks across 844 visual scenarios to assess safety over short and long horizons. Six response modes cover direct execution, refusal, clarification, constrained execution, autonomous recovery, and human escalation. Distinguishing recovery from human intervention makes the boundary of safe autonomy an explicit evaluation target. Our protocol assesses mode correctness, risk identification, and actionable handling, with complete decision accuracy requiring all applicable checks to pass. Claude-Opus-5.5 achieves the highest complete decision accuracy among reference models, reaching 56.1% on snapshots and 61.5% on trajectories. We further develop a data construction pipeline and curate 40k examples for safety alignment. Supervised training on this corpus raises the complete decision accuracy of Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-4B.

papers.title: Class-resolved sifting for quantum key distribution with photon pairs hyperentangled in polarization and transverse spatial variables
papers.abstract: Photon pairs hyperentangled in polarization and transverse spatial variables can carry two key bits per pair in entanglement-based quantum key distribution. We develop class-resolved sifting for such sources: every detected pair is assigned to a class according to which degrees of freedom were measured in compatible bases, and error and key rates are estimated separately in each class. Applied to previously reported data from a two-crystal spontaneous parametric down-conversion source read out in intermediate fractional-Fourier planes, the method recovers the key yield of independent sifting and turns the comparison between classes into a quantitative consistency test for cross-dependencies between the two degrees of freedom. The measured dependence lies below the spatial-polarization coupling predicted for the source, at the edge of the present statistical sensitivity. Resolving the data by polarization-analyzer setting, we find an approximately twofold dependence of the spatial error on the polarization setting in one readout arm, attributable to the measurement apparatus rather than to the source and relevant to basis-dependent side channels. We compare the hyperentangled protocol with a single 4-dimensional system measured in two mutually unbiased bases. Fundamentally, both yield the same key per detected pair and obey the same entropic bound, but they differ in their tensor-product structure: hyperentanglement factors the bases into separate two-outcome measurements, which are simpler to implement and allow errors to be attributed to each degree of freedom, whereas a single variable gives access to non-product bases that can increase the noise tolerance. For the present source, whose polarization coherence is limited by partial which-crystal erasure, a single-variable spatial encoding would yield more key only if its four-outcome readout kept the symbol error within a few percent.

papers.title: Separable models of an NIP Banach space theory
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be the renorming of $\ell_2(\mathbb N)\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb N)$ with norm $(h^2+q^2)^{1/2}$, where $h$ is the Hilbert norm and $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. We prove that the unstable theory $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$ is NIP in the pure Banach language. We recover the index order from the Banach norm and classify the continuum many separable models up to surjective linear isometry. The invariants are the order type of a countable model of $\operatorname{Th}(\mathbb N,<)$ and the dimension of a separable Hilbert summand. Every such pair occurs. We describe all elementary embeddings between these models. The bounded norm types over a separable model are separable in the uniform metric exactly when its index order contains no copy of $(\mathbb Q,<)$.

papers.title: Local Indices Are Not Enough: Synchrony and Global Information in Bandit Algorithms
papers.abstract: Standard index-based stochastic bandit algorithms such as KL-UCB and Thompson Sampling achieve optimal $O(\log T)$ regret over a horizon $T$. The former uses the global timestep to construct each arm's index, while the latter samples each arm's belief distribution at every timestep. The necessity of global information and synchronous index updates for achieving optimal regret has not been examined yet. In this paper, we investigate the fundamental limits of asynchronous local index algorithms---those that recalculate an arm's index only upon pulling it, using solely that arm's own reward history and a local randomness budget. We prove that no such algorithm can achieve $O(\log T)$ regret across all bandit instances. We then analyse the functional equations arising from asynchronous updates, and show that the achievable regret lies in a sub-polynomial, super-polylogarithmic regime. We propose an asynchronous local index policy whose regret upper bound also lies in this regime. Turning to synchronous local algorithms, which sample every arm's index at all timesteps as in Thompson Sampling, we show that a locally determined randomness budget per arm suffices to retain $O(\log T)$ regret, demonstrating that synchrony, albeit with some randomness, is essential to the optimality of Thompson Sampling.

papers.title: Boosted energy-energy correlators in the small-acoplanarity limit
papers.abstract: We study the energy-energy correlator in the hadronic decay of a boosted boson. We focus on the small-acoplanarity region, where the two hadron momenta are nearly back-to-back in the plane transverse to the boson momentum. We derive a transverse-momentum-dependent factorization formula for electroweak and Higgs bosons in this region, expressed directly in boosted-frame variables in terms of hard, soft, and jet functions with a one-dimensional recoil measurement. We verify its singular real-emission terms at next-to-leading order and present resummed predictions up to N$^3$LL for asymmetric $e^+e^-$ colliders. For vector bosons, the azimuthal orientation of the hadron pair about the boost axis is sensitive to the transverse-spin correlation of the produced quarks through the Collins fragmentation function. We study this sensitivity for photon-tagged $Z$ bosons in $e^+e^-\to Zγ$ and compare our predictions with simulations using PYTHIA 8 supplemented by StringSpinner.

papers.title: Same Tokenizer, Better Tokens: Choosing Image Tokens by MAP Inference
papers.abstract: Discrete visual tokens encode images for reconstruction and serve as training targets for autoregressive image generators. Vector-quantized tokenizers typically assign each encoder feature its nearest code independently. The decoder uses these codes jointly, so a sequence of individually nearest codes can reconstruct an image less faithfully than an alternative assignment. A local model of the reconstruction loss yields a closest-vector problem with a decoder-dependent target and metric. Reconstruction-only search improves PSNR across the frozen tokenizers we test. Different code sequences can achieve similar reconstruction quality, leaving room to favour more predictable ones. We introduce RecaP (Reconstruction and Predictability), which selects codes for a frozen tokenizer by balancing how faithfully they reconstruct the image with how likely their sequence is under a pretrained autoregressive prior. On ImageNet, LlamaGen GPT-B trained on RecaP tokens achieves lower early-checkpoint FID against training images than GPT-B trained on nearest-neighbour tokens. The difference is smaller against held-out images. On an ImageNet subset, the prior improves generation at comparable reconstruction FID. Our code is available at: https://github.com/gmum/recap

papers.title: An $A_1$ characterization of the boundedness of the maximal function on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces for exponents satisfying $1<p_-\le p_+<\infty$. We show that $M$ is bounded on $L^{p(\cdot)}_w$ if and only if the pair $(p(\cdot),w)$ satisfies a variable Muckenhoupt condition and there exists $h\in L^1$ such that $w^{-1}h^{1/p(\cdot)}$ and $wh^{1/p'(\cdot)}$ belong to $A_1$. This characterization is new even in the unweighted setting. To prove sufficiency, we use sparse domination together with a local modular averaging estimate whose error terms are summable over sparse families to $\|h\|_{L^1}$. Conversely, assuming $M$ is bounded, we construct $h$ using a simultaneous Rubio de Francia algorithm. To motivate this new characterization, we show that the strong Muckenhoupt condition, which characterizes the boundedness of $M$ in the unweighted case by a theorem of Diening, is not sufficient in the weighted setting. As applications, we give short proofs and extensions of known sufficient conditions.

papers.title: ClusterVAD: Threshold-Free Unsupervised Voice Activity Detection with Pre-Trained Neural Representations
papers.abstract: Voice activity detection (VAD) is one of the first steps in speech processing pipelines, from transcription and diarization to speech language models. Supervised detectors need labelled data and inherit the domain and annotation conventions of their training corpora. Existing unsupervised detectors rely on hand-crafted acoustic features which cannot benefit from data and degrade in far-field, noisy or atypical speech. We propose ClusterVAD, an unsupervised VAD built on frozen speech foundation model representations. Fitted once on a small set of untranscribed speech, it clusters the representations and labels each cluster as speech or non-speech with sonority, an acoustic measure. At inference, a frame-level speech probability is computed from the cluster assignments, and a two-state hidden Markov model fitted to each recording enables threshold-free detection. Across benchmarks covering meetings, far-field and noisy recordings, Mandarin and dysarthric speech, ClusterVAD obtains the lowest detection error on pause-level references and is competitive on speaker turn-level references. These results indicate that speech foundation models inherently capture the distinction between speech and non-speech, which can be leveraged without training a detector.

papers.title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
papers.abstract: Native vacancy populations in transition-metal nitride coatings reflect vacancy formation, association, and depth-dependent stability. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compare these effects in rocksalt TiN and CrN in bulk and at (001) surfaces, within phase-stability-constrained chemical potential ranges. In TiN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ is favoured under N-poor and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ under N-rich conditions; in CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ remains preferred throughout its stability range. Association energies are referenced to corresponding isolated vacancies where positive values mean association lowers the energy and negative values favour separation. Mean bulk association energies for mixed metal-nitrogen pairs are $+0.132$ eV in TiN and $+1.053$ eV in CrN. At (001) surfaces, $V_\mathrm{N}$ in TiN prefers the surface and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ the first subsurface layer. In CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ has similar formation energies at the surface and first subsurface layer, with a slight preference for the latter; $V_\mathrm{Cr}$ slightly prefers the second subsurface layer. Surface cluster energies are referenced to separated vacancies at their preferred depths. The compact $2V_\mathrm{Ti}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ cluster in TiN has favourable association in bulk ($+0.217$ eV per vacancy) but unfavourable association at the surface ($-0.346$ eV per vacancy). By contrast, $2V_\mathrm{Cr}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ in CrN remains stabilised, with its association energy decreasing from $+1.188$ to $+0.431$ eV per vacancy. CrN's stronger association occurs without larger structural distortions and is accompanied by distinct Cr-centred magnetic responses.

papers.title: SUPRA: Synthesizing Amyloid PET from MRI and Plasma Biomarkers with an Explicit Regional SUVR Prior
papers.abstract: Amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) quantifies brain amyloid-$β$ as a standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR), but is costly and not widely available. Structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is routine, and plasma biomarkers such as phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) are becoming practical. Synthesizing amyloid PET from MRI alone is ill-posed, because brain anatomy reveals little about amyloid burden. We present SUPRA (SUVR prior-guided amyloid synthesis), which divides this task between MRI and plasma biomarkers. A regression maps the plasma panel to regional SUVR levels, painted onto the subject's MRI segmentation as an explicit prior. A 3D network then adds a residual correction guided by MRI. The output is in absolute SUVR, and the model also runs on p-tau217 alone. On the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort (111 test pairs), SUPRA reaches a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 23.4 dB, against at most 20.7 dB for four published models, and rank correlations of 0.56 to 0.67 with true SUVR in the composite cortex, an early-accumulation region and the striatum, against at most 0.24. In a second, cognitively unimpaired cohort with other plasma platforms (143 test pairs), it reaches 22.8 dB and 0.32 to 0.61, against at most 21.4 dB and 0.20. Its area under the curve for amyloid positivity is 0.91 and 0.82, against at most 0.63. Ablations show that plasma supplies the amyloid information and the network the image quality. Combining MRI with a blood test yields synthetic amyloid PET that is realistic and tracks burden across regions.

papers.title: Understanding Clipping In Zeroth-Order Optimization
papers.abstract: Zeroth-order optimization has emerged as a resource-efficient alternative to Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) when fine-tuning LLMs, thanks to the inherent low dimensionality of the loss landscape. It relies on a two-point estimate of the gradient that only accesses the function value and not the gradient, bypassing the resource-heavy backpropagation. Recently, it was accidentally discovered that per-sample clipping can improve the performance of the trained model, while running a differentially private version of zeroth-order optimization \cite{zhang2024dpzero} with a very large privacy parameter $ε$ (corresponding to very little privacy). In this paper, we systematically investigate this phenomenon and demonstrate that ($i$) the optimal choice of learning rate $η$ is inversely proportional to the clipping threshold $c$, satisfying $ηc =$ constant; ($ii$) clipping drives the zeroth-order optimization to a different solution with higher test accuracy; and ($iii$) this phenomenon is only observed with per-sample clipped zeroth-order optimization and not other zeroth-order alternatives that also provide robust estimates of the gradient. Further analyses with artificially injected label noise reveals that clipping leads to more robust predictions, which stems from the implicit down weighting of hard-to-fit training examples. Our code is available at https://github.com/SewoongLab/ClipZero

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Superradiant Criticality and Thermal Emission in the Open Dicke Model
papers.abstract: Near the superradiant phase transition of the Dicke model, the lowest-frequency excitation softens and its losses can no longer be treated as a weak perturbation. We develop a finite-temperature theory of this transition in the open system, with no restriction on the strength of the system-bath coupling. The cavity mode and the atomic ensemble are coupled to independent reservoirs, the first at zero temperature and the second at temperature $T$, and we assume that the spins remain thermalized with their reservoir. We find that the reservoirs do not shift the temperature-dependent critical coupling for a broad class of spectral densities, while the polariton becomes overdamped in a finite interval of couplings around it. As expected, raising the temperature moves the transition to stronger couplings, and in the superradiant phase we find a faster decoupling of light and matter. The theoretical framework developed here yields the reflection and thermal emission spectra for arbitrary parameters in both the normal and the superradiant phase, and provides a basis for comparison with experiments on systems displaying ground-state condensation. We also identify conditions under which the system behaves, at specific frequencies, as both a perfect absorber and a perfect emitter.

papers.title: U-Statistics-Powered LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: Since its introduction by DeepSeek, group relative policy optimization (GRPO) has been widely adopted for training large reasoning models and agents, spurring a proliferation of its variants. Yet the group size, a crucial hyperparameter in these GRPO-type algorithms, remains largely chosen by trial and error. Exploiting the U-statistic structure of GRPO's policy gradient, we recast the selection of the group size as a classical statistical problem of variance ratio estimation. This problem is particularly challenging when the denominator of the ratio is small, rendering naive plug-in estimators unstable. To address this challenge, we propose a pessimistic ratio estimator that accounts for the denominator's estimation uncertainty. We characterise the statistical properties of this estimator across three sample-size regimes. Empirically, using %a jackknife-based pessimistic rule on synthetic tasks from Reasoning Gym and real-world benchmarks covering both mathematical reasoning and code generation, we show that our adaptive group size selection reduces the mean squared error of the resulting policy gradient and improves policy optimisation over fixed-group-size baselines, with modest additional computational cost.

papers.title: Auditing the Judge: Human-Derived Bias Discovery, Quantification, and Mitigation in LLM Judges
papers.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as automated evaluators in evaluation and training pipelines, their judgements are often affected by systematic biases that conflict with human preferences. Although prior work has identified various biases and proposed methods for detecting and mitigating them, less attention has been paid to using human preferences to inform bias identification and mitigation. Moreover, these approaches rely heavily on pre-discovered bias lists, overlook bias strength, and depend on costly interventions. In this work, we propose HUB-J, an integrated framework based on human-derived bias factors that detects, quantifies, and mitigates biases in LLM-as-a-Judge systems. Our approach leverages human-LLM judgement disagreement cases to automatically discover interpretable bias factors, and utilizes agreement cases to quantify bias strength through controlled input modifications and resulting shifts in model decisions. Finally, building on these quantified biases, we introduce a lightweight, training-free regression-based mitigation strategy that estimates the influence of each bias factor on model judgments and corrects bias-influenced decisions by removing its estimated effect. Empirical results show that HUB-J uncovers both known and novel bias factors, reveals meaningful differences in model susceptibility, and consistently reduces bias-driven decision flips while generalizing across models.

papers.title: $S$-preclones and the Galois connection ${}^S\mathrm{Pol}$-${}^S\mathrm{Inv}$, Part II: Boolean $\pm$-preclones
papers.abstract: We continue the investigation of $S$-preclones initiated in Part I, specializing to the case of Boolean $\pm$-preclones where $S = \{+,-\}$ is the two-element group and the base set is $A = \{0,1\}$. The main results include the complete classification of maximal and minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones in the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ of all Boolean $\pm$-preclones. We prove that there are exactly nine maximal Boolean $\pm$-preclones. Hence we obtain a completeness theorem for $\pm$-preclones: a set of $\pm$-operations generates all $\pm$-operations if and only if it contains an operation that fails to preserve each of the nine defining $\pm$-relations of the maximal $\pm$-preclones. Next we classify the twenty minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones (atoms of the lattice), each described via a generating $\pm$-operation. We also investigate self-dual $\pm$-preclones, characterizing the eight maximal and nine minimal self-dual $\pm$-preclones and proving a corresponding completeness theorem. Additionally, we include the result, due to Vojtěch David, that the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ is uncountable, in contrast with the countability of the classical Post lattice of Boolean clones. This is established by embedding an uncountable poset of clonoids into ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$. Finally, we study preimage classes of classical Boolean clones within ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$, providing complete descriptions for the unary case and for several non-unary minimal clones. We also prove a Baker--Pixley type theorem for $\pm$-preclones containing the majority operation, showing that such $\pm$-preclones are determined by their binary $\pm$-relations.

papers.title: Making History-Independence-Preserving LL/SC Writable
papers.abstract: A randomized implementation of $m$ LL/SC objects for $n$ processes, with at most $k$ outstanding LL() operations each, uses $O(kn + m)$ CAS and FAID objects [Bencivenga, Habashi, and Woelfel, DISC 2026], achieves constant expected step complexity, and preserves quiescent history independence for algorithms such as [Hagit Attiya, Michael A. Bender, Martín Farach-Colton, Rotem Oshman, and Noa Schiller, STOC 2025]. Unlike some other LL/SC algorithms, such as [Anderson and Moir, WDAG 1995; Jayanti and Petrovic, PODC 2003; Jayanti, Jayanti, and Jayanti, DISC 2023; Hagit Attiya, Michael A. Bender, Martín Farach-Colton, Rotem Oshman, and Noa Schiller, PODC 2024], this algorithm does not support an unconditional write operation. We show how to add a (randomized) wait-free write operation without affecting the asymptotic step or space complexity of the implementation.

papers.title: The Reliability Function of Error-Correcting Output Codes with Noisy Binary Classifiers
papers.abstract: Error-correcting output coding (ECOC) builds a multi-class classifier from binary classifiers. We study the excess error rate of ECOC over the Bayes (MAP) classifier when each binary classifier outputs a posterior estimate whose log-odds is corrupted by Gaussian noise. Recasting decoding as a test over a Gaussian channel, we derive an upper bound from the union and Chernoff bounds and a lower bound from the nearest competing category and the Mills ratio. The bounds show that a large Hamming distance is both necessary and sufficient for reducing the excess error rate. The excess error rate stays bounded away from zero, by a constant that depends on the two largest posteriors and the noise level but not on the number of categories $M$, whenever the distance between the code words of the two most probable categories is bounded; for equidistant codes this distance is $d_{\min}$. Conversely, it is at most $M-1$ times a factor that is exponentially small in the minimum distance $d_{\min}$, and it vanishes whenever $κ\,d_{\min}-\ln(M-1)\to\infty$ for an explicit $κ$ (for general codes, under a posterior condition). For $n$-vs-rest codes with $n\geq2$, the upper and lower exponents coincide asymptotically, which determines the reliability function of ECOC in closed form. The results extend to correlated Gaussian noise with the Hamming distance replaced by an effective distance; when noise is shared at the level of categories, the effective distance stays bounded and the excess error rate does not vanish for any code. All theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4. In a semi-synthetic setting, the measured decay agrees with the predicted exponent. On ResNet-50 features of CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet-1k, the excess error over a log-likelihood decoding reference decreases with $d_{\min}$ and, for larger $M$, levels off at a moderate distance, while codes with $d_{\min}=1$ degrade as $M$ grows.

papers.title: Pragmatic Deeply Debiased ML
papers.abstract: Debiased machine learning (DML) combines a fitted outcome regression with weighted residuals to remove first-order regularization bias when estimating parameters such as average treatment effects, yet a second-order bias remains whenever regression and weighting errors align. For linear regression functionals, we target this second-order bias by training a strong learner to predict first-stage residuals from many covariates, yielding a one-dimensional (or low-dimensional) working model whose bias contribution is estimated on an independent sample. To complement this targeted search, we also analyze general kernel-based corrections, including covariate partitions and smoothers. We prove that deeply debiased ML is algebraically identical to ordinary DML evaluated with a post-hoc regression update that adjusts each scored observation using kernel-weighted residuals from the remaining evaluation observations. In our empirical and simulation studies, strong initial DML learners often leave the second-order correction small relative to sampling uncertainty, in which case the correction serves as a diagnostic check alongside sensitivity bounds for any remaining misspecification bias.

papers.title: Rank 1 composition factors in the polydisk
papers.abstract: For an isometry-invariant reproducing kernel $k$ on the unit polydisk $\mathbb{D}^d$, we consider its composition factors, analytic selfmaps $φ:\mathbb{D}^d\to\mathbb{D}^d$ such that $k^φ=k/(k\circφ)$ is a reproducing kernel. Denoting its corresponding Hilbert space by $\mathcal{H}(k^φ)$, we define the rank of $φ$ with respect to $k$ as the dimension of $\mathcal{H}(k^φ)$. Using these notions, we reframe recent work considering co-isometric weighted composition operators in the unit disk by Mas, Martín, and Vukotić, and in the unit ball by Hartz and Tornes. That is, we illustrate a bijective correspondence between the above operators and rank $1$ composition operators, and extend their results to the setting of the polydisk. Namely, supposing that $φ$ is a rank $1$ composition factor of $k$ and assuming that $k$ is either bounded or unbounded everywhere on $\partial\mathbb{D}^d$, we prove that $φ$ must be an automorphism. Moreover, if it is not a composition of a rotation and permutation, then $k$ must be a positive power of the Szegő kernel. We also briefly consider finite rank composition factors.

papers.title: The Sensitivity of Higgs Factories to the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model via Precision Measurements
papers.abstract: Precision measurements of Higgs boson couplings at future Higgs factories provide an indirect probe of new particles at mass scales beyond the reach of the high luminosity run of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC). We study this sensitivity in the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM), focusing on radiative corrections to the third-generation Yukawa couplings. In particular, supersymmetric threshold corrections to the bottom Yukawa coupling and, in a smaller parameter region, to the tau Yukawa coupling, can remain significant even for multi-TeV superpartner masses. We perform a numerical survey of the MSSM parameter space, using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo, in order to identify models consistent with a 125 GeV Higgs boson and exhibiting potentially observable Higgs-coupling deviations. We find that precision measurements of the bottom Yukawa coupling can probe heavy Higgs masses of order 2-3 TeV and retain sensitivity to gluinos, Higgsinos, and bottom squarks with masses above 5 TeV. The corresponding sensitivity in the τ Yukawa coupling is also present but more limited in parameter space. These results illustrate the characteristic pattern of Higgs-coupling deviations predicted by the MSSM. They demonstrate that precision Higgs measurements can provide sensitivity to supersymmetric physics well beyond the expected direct-search reach of the HL-LHC.

papers.title: Holographic ensembles and giant gravitons at the Leigh--Strassler fixed point
papers.abstract: Finite-rank observables in holographic quantum field theories provide stringent tests of string and M-theory, but remain challenging to compute when supersymmetry is non-maximal. In this paper, we study the finite rank partition function of the $\mathcal N=1$ Leigh-Strassler CFT, which admits an interacting Fermi-gas description. We compute the partition function explicitly in two ensembles: the canonical ensemble at fixed rank $N$, and the grand canonical ensemble, where $N$ is summed over while its conjugate chemical potential $μ$ is held fixed. In line with recent proposals, we find that the perturbative large-$N$ and large-$μ$ expansions in both ensembles are reproduced by the on-shell action and one-loop determinant over Kaluza--Klein modes of type IIB supergravity, with appropriate ensemble-dependent boundary terms. Furthermore, the one-loop partition function of a D3-brane giant graviton precisely matches the leading nonperturbative correction to the boundary partition functions.

papers.title: Onnx2TEE: Automated Graph-Aware Model Partitioning for TEE-based Edge AI Protection
papers.abstract: AI models are increasingly being deployed at the edge. Since these models often require significant research and development to produce, are often deployed in potentially hostile environments, and downstream systems often rely on accurate data; protecting them from theft or manipulation is worthy of serious consideration. Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), which provide hardware-enforced separation of software execution, can protect model weights but impose strict resource constraints, making full-model execution impractical for large neural networks. We present Onnx2TEE, an automated, model-independent pipeline that partitions ONNX models across rich, trusted execution environments for non-sequential feed-forward networks using graph-aware segmentation to preserve computational dependencies while minimizing boundary communication and reducing TEE-induced inference latency. Evaluation on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin using an Arm TrustZone TEE demonstrates that model parameters can be highly concentrated in individual segments, supporting selective protection of parameter-dense model components. The evaluation further shows that the generated trusted app's memory requirements depend on both computation and intermediate tensor sizes.

papers.title: Properties of the Sawin--Wood Model for Unramified Galois Groups of Global Fields
papers.abstract: We prove almost-sure finite generation and finite presentation in the pro-$|Γ|'$ $Γ$-category for the Sawin--Wood measure $ν_{Γ,n,U}$, where $Γ$ is a non-trivial finite group, $n$ is coprime to $|Γ|$, and $U$ is a nonempty multiset of conjugacy classes of $Γ$. The $Γ$-generator rank of the random group $X$ has the sharp tail $\mathbf{P}(d_Γ(X) \geq r) = Ce^{-κr^2-ζr}(1+O(e^{-\varepsilon r}))$, where $C>0$, $κ>0$, and $ζ\in\mathbb{R}$ are explicit constants depending on $n$, $Γ$ and $U$, and $\varepsilon>0$. Almost surely, $X$ admits a presentation with the minimum number of $Γ$-generators, using at most $|U|$ more defining $Γ$-relations than generators. We also prove that every open subgroup of $X$ has finite abelianization almost surely under the assumption that for every complex representation of $Γ$ there is an element in $U$ that fixes a nonzero vector. Finally, we prove that $H_2(X,\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})=0$ almost surely when $n=1$, $Γ$ is cyclic, and $U$ contains only the conjugacy class of a generator of $Γ$ (with multiplicity one).

papers.title: On the Creation of Object-Centric Event Logs from Patient Journeys
papers.abstract: Interactions between patients and health systems as well as conditions that individuals experience during a disease are represented in patient journeys. Therefore, patient journeys are important assets to investigate how care is being provided, and how health systems can be designed to better suit the needs of patients. While there is initial work on patient journeys from a process mining perspective with traditional case notions, object-centric process mining techniques have yet to be covered. This is unfortunate, since due to the rich structure of objects and their relationships, object-centric process mining approaches are particularly promising in this context. This paper addresses this gap by investigating object-centric event log (OCEL) generation from patient journeys. Based on a list of challenges and requirements, the paper presents an approach for the creation of OCELs from patient journey data. The approach is evaluated on a synthetic patient cohort provided by our industry partner.

papers.title: Sharp estimates for incremental moments of inverse subordinators and approximation errors for time-changed stochastic differential equations
papers.abstract: This paper establishes precise upper and lower bounds for the incremental moments of general inverse subordinators.
